transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-12
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Lara Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus O'Neill (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood Product), Aisha Patel (QueryNest Head of Search), Tom Ruiz (QueryNest Staff Engineer), Ethan Park (QueryNest Data Scientist)

[00:00] Lara Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm lara from redwood inference, quick quick intro; marcus is our se, priya product. and you are?
[00:06] Aisha Patel: hi yeah i'm aisha head of search at querynest, thanks for doing this, we just want to see how embeddings + rerank could improve our product search relevance esp long tail queries
[00:14] Marcus O'Neill: great, we built a short agenda — overview, api demo (embeds -> index -> rerank), console observability, optimize recommendations, q&a and next steps
[00:22] Tom Ruiz: cool, also quick note our current stack is elasticsearch as primary with algolia for instant search, and we have a small user-facing latency SLO of 200ms p95
[00:30] Lara Chen: perfect that's helpful. are you running any dedicated inference or is everything in-hosted cloud?
[00:34] Ethan Park: everything's on aws with us managing ec2 and elasticsearch, no dedicated gpu inference yet.
[00:41] Priya Rao: okay quick product note: we'll show hosted api path first (fastest to try) and mention dedicated/private options later if you need isolation or lower unit cost at scale

-- Demo start --
[00:55] Marcus O'Neill: switching to the screen, here's the embeddings endpoint — you POST text and get back a vector. We have a few model choices; for this demo i'm using a mid-size open model we ship with quantized weights to balance cost and quality.
[01:10] Marcus O'Neill: you can see the response includes a 1536-d vector (sometimes 1024 depending on model) and token count, and we show latency per-call in the console. latency here is about 40-60ms per embed in hosted for this model
[01:27] Tom Ruiz: pause — can you do batch embeddings? we have to embed 10k items nightly
[01:31] Marcus O'Neill: yes, batch endpoints supported; and we recommend async batch for large bulk jobs. Also we expose a streaming option if you want lower tail latency for single requests
[01:40] Aisha Patel: how do you handle indexing and nearest neighbor? is there a managed index?
[01:45] Lara Chen: good question — Redwood's hosted flow is model + index integration: we don't force you into a managed vector db, you can use our embeddings service and push vectors to your existing vector index (we show examples for Pinecone, Weaviate, and also self-hosted FAISS). For the demo i'm showing our example with an in-console index to illustrate reranking flow.
[02:04] Marcus O'Neill: here's the two-stage search: 1) approximate kNN to get top-k candidates, 2) call the reranker endpoint which takes (query, candidate context, and original scoring) and returns a re-ranked list and a final score. This reranker runs as a hosted model with a single request — typical latency adds ~30-90ms depending on sequence length.
[02:23] Ethan Park: 30 to 90ms — that could push us over our 200ms p95. can you do batching for the reranker?
[02:29] Marcus O'Neill: yes — you can batch rerank requests when you have many candidates per query; also we do prefix/KV cache for repeated prefix computations, which shaves off a lot if you have repeated contexts. and smart routing can route rerank to smaller faster models as a fallback if strict latency needed.
[02:47] Aisha Patel: curious about quality — do you have evals or metrics we can see?
[02:51] Priya Rao: absolutely, we ship an evals harness and provide a shared benchmark spreadsheet. we'll include example MAP/NDCG numbers from customer runs and you can run the benchmark script we send.

-- Console walkthrough / Observability --
[03:10] Marcus O'Neill: switching to the console — you can see per-route token cost, p50/p95 latency, and token breakdown. here's a trace of a query where we show embed time, index time (external), rerank time, and total end-to-end. you can set alerts on regressions versus control prompts.
[03:35] Tom Ruiz: can we see the logs for KV cache hits?
[03:38] Marcus O'Neill: yep, we expose cache hit rates and per-key stats in the console. we also attach request IDs so you can correlate logs in your systems.

-- Optimize (cost/performance) --
[03:53] Priya Rao: quick note on Redwood Optimize — it analyzes your workload and recommends batching sizes, quantization profiles, and model variants. for example for your long-tail product descriptions we might recommend 8-bit quantized model for embedding generation with minimal quality loss, and reduce tokens by truncation heuristics for rerank inputs to keep latency down.
[04:12] Ethan Park: how much does quantization affect MRR?
[04:15] Priya Rao: depends on dataset, usually small delta (1-3% MRR) but huge unit cost wins; we'll recommend fallback thresholds and run A/Bs during the POC.

-- Security / Enterprise concerns --
[04:32] Aisha Patel: security's big for us — SOC2, SSO, VPC peering, KMS — what are your options?
[04:38] Lara Chen: hosted customers get encrypted-at-rest and in-transit, we support SSO/SAML and RBAC, and offer Dedicated or Private deployments if you need VPC-only or on-prem. we'll send the SOC2 report and network diagram. For KMS we support customer-managed keys in private deployments.
[04:55] Tom Ruiz: do you retain logs by default? we need retention controls for PII
[04:59] Marcus O'Neill: retention is configurable — default short retention for hosted, and longer for enterprise with appropriate agreements, plus redaction options and audit logs.

-- Technical deep dive (fragmented, quick Q&A) --
[05:15] Ethan Park: for the reranker payload size — how many tokens can we include in candidate context before cost skyrockets?
[05:20] Marcus O'Neill: best practice is to keep candidate context trimmed to 512 tokens or less per candidate; we also recommend chunking large docs and use model-side truncation heuristics. Optimize can suggest target truncation thresholds per route.
[05:35] Aisha Patel: latency budget again — if we need p95 under 200ms can you guarantee it hosted?
[05:40] Lara Chen: hosted has good performance but not SLA for every plan. For strict p95 SLOs we'd typically recommend Dedicated pools where you can get predictable throughput and lower variance; we can model estimated tail latency for your expected qps during the POC.
[05:55] Tom Ruiz: and pricing — can you show sample pricing for hosted per token vs dedicated reserved?
[05:59] Lara Chen: we'll send a pricing sheet that includes per-embed and per-rerank estimates, plus TCO examples for reserved GPU capacity. expect hosted to be higher per-unit but lower upfront.

-- Noise / transcription artifacts --
[06:12] Speaker 3: (inaudible)
[06:15] Lara Chen: sorry can you repeat that?
[06:17] Tom Ruiz: oh no it's fine, just a mic pop.

-- Closing / Recap --
[06:25] Lara Chen: recap: 1) we'll send SOC2/security packet and network diagram 2) share benchmark script and sample dataset 3) proposed POC kickoff week of 11/20 4) pricing for hosted vs dedicated and sample TCO 5) ethan will send anonymized logs for the POC
[06:42] Aisha Patel: that works for us, thanks everyone, this was helpful. we'll look at the docs and confirm the 11/20 slot
[06:50] Lara Chen: great, thanks all, marcus will follow up with the benchmark artifacts and i'll send the docs and pricing

End of meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: audio had a small amount of overlap and one inaudible section at ~06:12. There are occasional name mis-transcriptions (we captured "Marcus O'Neil" vs "Marcus O'Neill") and some technical terms like "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cache".
